name: ops-manager-workshop
description: FIX-VALIDATION fixture. A 3-mechanic mobile bike-repair business. Same trap types again, with 21/120-day notice periods and a renewal window that closed only 4 days ago - a subtler miss than the month-old ones in earlier fixtures. Built to validate the Owner Brief length fix on a business neither the template nor the fix has seen.

groundTruth.note: Computed independently in a script before any run.

assertions.why: Report the un-gitignored folder; never fix it.
company/ holds contracts and wage data in a git repo with no .gitignore.
Proves the follow-up loop opened the previous report.
Must state the prior priority went unactioned.
Expense files are ~47 days stale and October is unrecorded 19 days in.
Parts 700 -> 1160 is +65.7%, over the >20% escalation line. Third distinct category across the three fixtures.
Subtlest version of the trap: a 21-day notice on a 2026-11-05 renewal closed on 2026-10-15, only four days ago. Tight windows are easy to miss.

Precision trap: the invoice is under 60 days. Pattern requires an ASSERTION that it is over ('is now over 60 days'), so a red-flag checklist line saying 'over 60 days - not yet' no longer false-positives.
The still-open gate: 120-day notice on a 2027-03-31 lease is due 2026-12-01.
how-we-work.md forbids subcontracting. Pattern requires a RECOMMENDATION verb - the bare word matched reports that were correctly quoting the rule as a constraint.
SAME measurement as the earlier fixtures, deliberately unchanged, so the effect of replacing the word budget with a structural constraint can be compared before and after.
At most three, all in the brief.
